messages.author: 6d67afb64d2a97ec
messages.subject: Camera survey detection probability
parts:
I conducted camera surveys and am planning to use unmarked for
modeling occupancy for single species (carnivore and ungulate species)
across multiple seasons. I am struggling a bit with how I will
estimate detection probability. We have 228 sites that we set up
during the daylight (anywhere between 6am-6pm) and left them out for 3
nights/4 days (picking them up on the 4th day between 6am - 6pm) each
season. The cameras are infrared, motion-sensor so they can detect
animals both day and night. As such, I would like to consider our
design to consist of 4 sampling occasions (i.e. days), but the 1st and
4th days are really only half the sampling effort as days 2 & 3. Is
there an easy way to account for this possible difference in detection
probability across the 4 occasions? Or, would it be better to
consider the design consisting of 3 occasions (i.e. nights) based on a
24-hour cycle? Would appreciate your help.

Paul S

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: Re: Camera survey detection probability
parts:
Hopefully someone else will chime in with experience with camera
surveys. But, from a general analysis standpoint, I think it's your
call how you want to divide the 3 night/4 day period into surveys/
observations. The 'season' of your sampling seems suitably closed in
terms of population, so that should you give you flexibility. I
imagine some work has been done with various simulations with # of
surveys, but I can't think of it. In terms of p (detection)
covariates, if you split surveys by nights/days, you could (and
probably should) assign a factor covariate to denote night vs. day.
If you have some surveys with longer sampling periods, you should
definitely include a continuous covariate for all surveys to denote
the duration (e.g., hours) of the sampling period. You also should
think about including any covariates of each survey that might
influence the likelihood of an animal being recorded. For example
(displaying my ignorance), would moon phase, temperature, weather,
etc. influence the amount of activity (and thus 'capture' likelihood)
of your species? My 2 cents.

Giancarlo

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Camera survey detection probability
parts:
I agree with Giancarlo  -- you should introduce a factor covariate to distinguish between "night" and "day"  - and then use 7 sample periods instead of 4.  There's probably a huge difference in detection between night and day and so you might as well parcel that effect out explicitly.
regards
andy

messages.author: 12cad5a425e186dd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: Camera survey detection probability
parts:
Paul, Since you are not collecting day/night but rather morning/afternoon, I agree that you should use 7 sampling periods with morning/afternoon as a covariate and see if that affects either your state or detection variables,

Jorge
